Even for historical 1.x conda-forge builds listed in affected_versions, the vulnerable code path only exists when the separate Edge3 provider is installed on top of Airflow 2.x, which is a condition external to this package.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade airflow-with-virtualenv to version 2.3.0 or later (latest conda-forge version 2.10.5 is not affected). If using historical versions prior to 2.3.0, also ensure that the Apache Airflow Pinot Provider is updated to version 4.0.0 or later, as the vulnerability is triggered only when the Pinot Provider is installed.

Upgrade airflow-with-virtualenv to version 2.5.1 or later (latest conda-forge version 2.10.5 is not affected). If using historical versions prior to 2.5.1, also ensure that apache-airflow-providers-mysql is updated to 4.0.0 or later if it is installed, as the vulnerability also affects that provider.

Upgrade airflow-with-virtualenv to version 2.3.0 or later (latest conda-forge version 2.10.5 is not affected). If using historical versions prior to 2.3.0 and the Apache Airflow Pig Provider is installed, also update the Pig Provider to version 4.0.0 or later to remediate the vulnerability.

Upgrade to apache-airflow 2.3.0 or later on conda-forge (current latest is 3.2.2, which is unaffected). Additionally, if the apache-airflow-providers-pinot package is installed, upgrade it to version 4.0.0 or later. Historical conda-forge builds of airflow prior to 2.3.0 remain vulnerable when used with Pinot Provider < 4.0.0.

Upgrade to apache-airflow 2.5.1 or later on conda-forge (current latest is 3.2.2, which is unaffected). If the apache-airflow-providers-mysql package is installed, ensure it is upgraded to version 4.0.0 or later. Historical conda-forge builds of airflow prior to 2.5.1 remain vulnerable when used with MySQL Provider < 4.0.0.

Upgrade to apache-airflow 2.3.0 or later on conda-forge (current latest is 3.2.2, which is unaffected). If the apache-airflow-providers-pig package is installed, upgrade it to version 4.0.0 or later. Historical conda-forge builds of airflow prior to 2.3.0 remain vulnerable when used with Pig Provider < 4.0.0.

Upgrade apache-airflow-providers-apache-hive to version 5.0.0 or later (the latest conda-forge version is 9.5.0, which is not affected). All conda-forge builds prior to 5.0.0 listed in affected_versions are vulnerable to command injection.
Upgrade apache-airflow-providers-apache-sqoop to version 3.1.1 or later (latest conda-forge version is 4.2.1, which is not affected). Avoid using any conda-forge build older than 3.1.1.

Users running any apache-airflow-providers-edge3 version < 2.0.0 with Apache Airflow 2 should immediately uninstall the provider and migrate to Airflow 3. Upgrade to apache-airflow-providers-edge3 >= 2.0.0 (e.g., the latest conda-forge version 3.7.0), which requires Airflow 3 and has removed the RCE-prone Airflow 2 code paths. If already on Airflow 3 with Edge3, no action is required as the advisory does not affect that configuration.

Upgrade apache-airflow-providers-apache-hive to version 6.0.0 or later. The current conda-forge release (9.5.0) is not affected, but historical builds at versions 1.0.1 through 5.1.3 remain vulnerable.

Upgrade apache-airflow-providers-apache-hive to version 5.1.3 or later to remediate this vulnerability. The current conda-forge release (9.5.0) is not affected. Historical builds at versions 1.0.1 through 5.1.2 are vulnerable and should be upgraded.

Upgrade apache-airflow-providers-apache-hive to version 6.1.1 or later. The current conda-forge release (9.5.0) is not affected. Historical conda-forge builds at versions 1.0.1 through 6.1.0 remain vulnerable and should be upgraded immediately.

Upgrade apache-airflow-providers-google to version 8.10.0 or later (conda-forge latest is 19.1.0, which is fixed). Historical conda-forge builds prior to 8.10.0 remain vulnerable and should not be used in production environments.

Upgrade apache-airflow-providers-snowflake to version 6.4.0 or later (the latest conda-forge release is 6.13.0). Historical conda-forge builds at or below 6.3.1 are vulnerable to SQL/special-element injection via CopyFromExternalStageToSnowflakeOperator.

Upgrade apache-airflow-providers-mysql to version 4.0.0 or later (the latest conda-forge version 6.6.1 is not affected). Any conda-forge installation of versions 1.0.1 through 3.4.0 remains vulnerable and should be updated immediately.

Upgrade CKAN to a version >= 2.9.9 (or 2.10.1 for the 2.10.x line) when those versions become available on conda-forge. Until then, consider restricting access to resource creation/editing endpoints or applying the upstream patches manually. Monitor the ckan-feedstock for an updated conda-forge release.

Upgrade the bentoml conda-forge package to version 1.2.5 or later (latest available: 1.4.39) to remediate this insecure deserialization vulnerability. Historical conda-forge builds prior to 1.2.5 remain vulnerable.

Upgrade apache-airflow to version 2.3.0 or later (latest conda-forge version 3.2.2 is not affected). If using an older conda-forge build, also ensure apache-airflow-providers-apache-pinot is upgraded to 4.0.0 or later. Historical conda-forge builds 2.0.1–2.2.5 remain vulnerable if the Pinot provider is installed.

Upgrade apache-airflow to version 2.5.1 or later (latest conda-forge version 3.2.2 is not affected). If using an older conda-forge build (2.0.1–2.5.0), also ensure apache-airflow-providers-mysql is upgraded to 4.0.0 or later. Historical conda-forge builds in the vulnerable range should be replaced.

Upgrade apache-airflow to version 2.3.0 or later (latest conda-forge version 3.2.2 is not affected). If using an older conda-forge build (2.0.1–2.2.5), also ensure apache-airflow-providers-apache-pig is upgraded to 4.0.0 or later. Historical conda-forge builds in the vulnerable range remain affected if the Pig provider is installed.
Users running bentoml 1.3.18 from conda-forge should upgrade to 1.4.39 (or any version >= 1.4.3) which contains the fix for this insecure pickle deserialization vulnerability in serde.py.

Users running any bentoml conda-forge version prior to 1.4.8 should upgrade to 1.4.39 (the current latest conda-forge release), which is beyond the fixed point of 1.4.8 and is not vulnerable to this runner server insecure deserialization issue.

Users running any bentoml conda-forge version at or below 1.4.5 (as listed in affected_versions) should upgrade to 1.4.39, which is the latest conda-forge release and is believed to be beyond the vulnerable range based on related advisory GHSA-7v4r-c989-xh26 (fixed at 1.4.8).

statements.impact_statement: The CVE-2024-28423 advisory was incorrectly attributed to the PyPI 'diagrams' package (mingrammer/diagrams); the vulnerability exists in the entirely separate 'airflow-diagrams' package (pkg:pypi/airflow-diagrams). The conda-forge 'diagrams' package does not contain the vulnerable cli.py unsafe_load code from airflow-diagrams and is therefore not affected.

This advisory was withdrawn because the described pickle-based deserialization behavior is intentional and documented in Dask Distributed's known limitations. Dask explicitly states its distributed scheduler is not designed for untrusted network access; exposing it to the public internet is a misconfiguration, not a vulnerability in the dask-core package itself. No conda-forge versions should be considered affected by this withdrawn advisory.

This advisory was withdrawn because it describes intended behavior: Dask Distributed's use of pickle serialization is a documented design decision and known security trade-off documented at https://distributed.dask.org/en/stable/limitations.html. The Dask security model assumes trusted workers and clients; no patch is expected or warranted. The advisory is not a valid vulnerability for any conda-forge version of dask.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to duckdb >= 0.9.3 on conda-forge (latest: 1.5.3) to remediate the malicious extension injection vulnerability. Avoid using untrusted or unverified DuckDB extensions with older builds.

This is a withdrawn duplicate of GHSA-832w-fhmw-w4f4. Users should upgrade to dtale >= 3.17.0 (latest conda-forge: 3.22.0) to resolve the underlying command injection vulnerability. Tracking should be moved to the canonical advisory GHSA-832w-fhmw-w4f4.

Upgrade to gdal >= 3.0.2 on conda-forge (latest is 3.13.1). Historical conda-forge builds 2.4.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.4, and 3.0.1 are vulnerable to a double-free in OGRExpatRealloc; users running those versions should upgrade immediately.
